lessons.title: Lesson 1: Introduction to Design Thinking Principles
lessons.description: In this lesson, students will explore the core principles of design thinking, including empathy, prototyping, and iterative testing. They will also delve into the innovation process, identifying areas of opportunity for innovation, and learn about interview techniques and user empathy-building. Students will understand how to mitigate validation risk using the Forge 231 Ovation Rubric through case studies. They will also study the importance of customer-centric innovation, including problem validation and customer discovery, understanding problem significance and incidence, and creating user personas and user stories. Students will participate in a customer development process, including customer interviews and field visits. The lesson will introduce the concept of Minimum Usable Prototype (MUP), design a value proposition, and test it. Students will also explore concept generation, solution exploration, and concept design, including the evaluation of technology alternatives and solution concepts. Finally, the lesson will cover system thinking and understanding complex systems.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Design Thinking Principles and Empathy
lessons.description: In this lesson, students explore the core principles of design thinking, focusing on human-centered design and empathy-building techniques. They will engage in role-playing activities and group discussions to understand the innovation process, conduct interviews for empathy, and validate solutions using the Forge 231 Ovation Rubric. Students will also learn about user-centric innovation, including problem validation, customer discovery, and user personas, through case studies and the customer development process. Additionally, they will apply design thinking tools such as Minimum Usable Prototypes, value proposition design, and systematic concept generation to develop and test compelling solutions.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Validation and Case Studies
lessons.description: In this lesson, students will explore validation techniques such as the Forge 231 Ovation Rubric to mitigate risk and ensure successful innovation. Through case studies, students will analyze how validation can lead to successful solutions. The lesson covers the importance of user-centric innovation, including problem and customer validation, user personas, and the customer development process. Additionally, students will learn about the concept of Minimum Usable Prototype (MUP), design a compelling value proposition, and understand the systematic concept generation and evaluation process for solution concepts.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: MUP & Value Proposition Design
lessons.description: In this lesson, students will learn about the Minimum Usable Prototype (MUP) and how to create one. They will also explore and design a value proposition, including how to validate it effectively through customer interviews and field visits. The lesson will cover the importance of customer-centric innovation, including problem validation, user personas, and the customer development process. Students will also learn about concept generation and system thinking, focusing on understanding and evaluating solution concepts and technology alternatives.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: System Thinking & Concept Exploration
lessons.description: In this lesson, students will explore system thinking, understanding complex systems, and the process of generating and evaluating solution concepts. They will also learn about building a compelling value proposition and applying design thinking tools such as Minimum Usable Prototypes (MUP), designing and testing value propositions, and conducting customer development processes through interviews and field visits. Students will also learn about concept generation, including exploring and iterating on solution concepts, assessing feasibility, and evaluating technology alternatives and solution concepts.
